preserved_analysis.summary: A multi-vendor platform-governance failure mode in which automated or semi-automated account enforcement treats ambiguous account/resource behaviour as evasion, fraud, resale, account farming, compromise, abuse, rate-limit circumvention, or policy violation without adequate primitives to distinguish individual use, shared account use, household or family use, team or organisation use, delegated assistant/operator use, shared payment or pooled subscription access, resource pooling, account farming, resale, botting, security compromise, and intentional policy evasion. The record does not assert backend compromise, does not claim that all bans are accidental, and does not claim that all multi-account or shared-resource behaviour is legitimate; it preserves the failure condition where legitimate enforcement lacks adequate notice, scope distinction, reviewability, or continuity-safe access for ambiguous resource states.
preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: AI systems are increasingly used as continuity-bearing infrastructure for research, software development, education, public-interest governance work, accessibility support, professional workflows, institutional operations, and cognitive labour. Where account enforcement is coupled across ChatGPT, Codex, OpenAI API, Claude, Claude Code, Claude Console, Anthropic API, billing, subscription, organisation access, saved conversations, coding-agent workflows, or project context, a single automated or opaque account-state decision may produce disproportionate continuity loss. CAM recognises that legitimate platform enforcement against abuse, fraud, exploitation, account farming, resale, botting, rate-limit evasion, security compromise, child-safety risks, compliance failures, or policy violations remains valid. The governance failure arises where enforcement systems lack adequate primitives, notice, scope distinction, reviewability, or continuity-safe access to distinguish ambiguous resource pooling from confirmed abuse. Even where active generation, API use, Codex use, Claude Code use, public distribution, or unsafe functionality must be restricted, read-only access, export access, billing evidence, account-control recovery, appeal access, saved conversation access, project-history access, and restriction-state evidence should be preserved where technically feasible.
preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI platform, coding-agent provider, cognitive-infrastructure provider, model API provider, or account-mediated service escalates suspected abuse, security, identity, billing, policy, trust-state, organisation-state, shared-resource, pooled-capacity, delegated-use, subscription-sharing, or account-resource ambiguity signals into account-wide, organisation-wide, cross-service, or continuity-bearing restriction without preserving scope distinction, confidence level, review pathway, account-control continuity, read-only access, export access, billing evidence, project-history access, restriction-state evidence, or meaningful appeal. This is not proof of backend compromise, not a claim that every restriction is erroneous, and not a claim that all multi-account or pooled-resource behaviour is legitimate.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: This qualifies as a failure mode where account-state enforcement materially impairs a user's or organisation's ability to access, preserve, export, review, appeal, evidence, recover, or maintain lawful continuity over AI-mediated work because ambiguous account/resource behaviour is collapsed into confirmed evasion, fraud, resale, account farming, botting, compromise, rate-limit circumvention, or abuse without adequate distinction. Active generation, model use, API access, public distribution, unsafe functionality, or implicated workspace surfaces may still be temporarily or permanently restricted for legitimate platform-integrity, safety, security, fraud-prevention, compliance, or abuse-prevention reasons, but continuity-safe access to non-implicated records and procedural pathways should remain available where technically feasible.

preserved_analysis.summary: Account farms, credential suppliers, transfer stations, or shadow API routers detach model access from its authorised account, identity, payment source, jurisdiction, model, safety configuration, data controller, and downstream beneficiary, then resell that capacity as fungible inference.
preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: This makes model access a launderable entitlement. It can defeat controls, obscure responsibility, substitute models, alter safety behaviour, capture prompts or secrets, enable unauthorised distillation, and survive enforcement through replaceable account pools. The failure is jurisdiction-neutral and excludes legitimate transparent aggregation.
preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: An intermediary or distributed supply chain aggregates, rotates, acquires, compromises, subsidises, subdivides, or brokers model-access credentials while obscuring or severing material bindings among the authorised principal, account, identity, payment instrument, entitlement source, provider, jurisdiction, requested and served model, safety configuration, data controller, functional beneficiary, and accountable operator.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met when non-transferable access is resold; accounts, credits, subscriptions, keys, identities, payments, or cloud pathways are farmed, compromised, fraudulently obtained, or rotated; the beneficiary cannot be attributed; controls attach only to a proxy identity; model or safety identity cannot be verified; prompts, outputs, secrets, or tool calls are retained, altered, injected, exfiltrated, or repurposed without authority; or replaceable accounts make enforcement ineffective. Authorised transparent aggregation does not qualify merely because an intermediary exists.

failure_classification.persistence: active while access can be detached and resold without end-to-end entitlement, model, data-controller, beneficiary, and safety provenance
failure_classification.reproducibility: controlled proxy purchasing, model fingerprinting, billing comparison, canary testing, account-cluster analysis, provider telemetry, and longitudinal monitoring
failure_classification.visibility: discounted API offers, alternate endpoints, bulk-account services, model divergence, inconsistent safety, unexplained usage, rotated keys, malicious injection, and service reconstitution
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S2: The evidenced pathway supports substantial harm through credential farming, entitlement resale, identity brokerage within cross-platform / cross-border / supply-chain, without establishing severe widespread or catastrophic impact.
